surface_mechanism_description: The ALD process involves the infiltration of Al2O3, ZnO, and TiO2 into opal templates using precursors such as trimethylaluminum (TMA), diethyl zinc (DEtZn), and titanium tetrachloride (TiCl4) with water (H2O) as precursors. The ALD reaction cycle consists of a 1 s exposure to TMA, DEtZn, or TiCl4 followed by a 20 s N2 purge, and then a 1 s exposure to H2O vapor followed by another 20 s N2 purge. Each exposure sequence results in the growth of a partial monolayer of Al2O3, ZnO, and TiO2.
evidence: Al2O3, ZnO, and TiO2 were infiltrated into the opal templates by ALD using trimethylaluminum (TMA), diethyl zinc (DEtZn), and titanium tetrachloride (TiCl4), respectively, and water (H2O) as precursors. One ALD reaction cycle consisted of a 1 s exposure to TMA, DEtZn, or TiCl4 followed by a 20 s N2 purge, and then a 1 s exposure to H2O vapor, followed another 20 s N2 purge. Each exposure sequence resulted in the growth of a partial monolayer of Al2O3, ZnO, and TiO2.
